content: Jane E. Henney is an American physician who holds the distinction of being the first woman to serve as the Commissioner of the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA). She was appointed to this role by President Bill Clinton and served as Commissioner from 1998 to 2001. Prior to this, she had served at the FDA from 1992 to 1994 as the Deputy Commissioner for Operations under the leadership of then-Commissioner David Aaron Kessler, MD. Following her earlier tenure at the FDA, she held a leadership position at the University of New Mexico (UNM), where she served as Vice President of the Health Sciences Center. Dr. Henney was born in Woodburn, Indiana. She completed her undergraduate education at Manchester College and earned her Doctor of Medicine (MD) degree from the Indiana University School of Medicine. She pursued postgraduate training at The University of Texas MD Anderson Cancer Center in Houston, Texas, where she specialized in medical oncology. In 1976, she joined the National Cancer Institute (NCI), part of the National Institutes of Health (NIH), where she worked in the Cancer Therapy and Evaluation Program. Dr. Henney is married to James Robert Graham III, MD, who has also had a notable career as a physician and leader in the medical field. After her tenure at the FDA, she joined the board of directors of the pharmaceutical company AstraZeneca. In 2003, she was appointed as Senior Vice President and Provost for Health Affairs at the University of Cincinnati.
